definition: Prototype methods are machine learning methods that use data prototypes.
details: A data prototype is a data value that reflects other values in its class, e.g., the centroid in a K-means clustering problem.

explainer.lead: These methods classify by comparing new points to representative examples of each class, which makes decisions interpretable and cheap.

tiers.eli5: Instead of memorising every student, you pick one typical student per group and ask which one a newcomer resembles most.
tiers.practitioner: They are used where explainability and low latency matter, such as nearest-prototype classifiers; a pitfall is that a poor choice of prototypes, like a centroid split across clusters, misrepresents the class.
tiers.paperLevel: A prototype is a data value reflecting others in its class, such as the K-means centroid; limits arise when classes are multimodal, since one prototype cannot capture several modes.

explainer.example: In K-means clustering, the centroid of each cluster serves as its prototype, and a new point is assigned to the nearest centroid.
